name: Gedaliah
overview: Gedaliah was a male Levite, uniquely identified as the son of Jeduthun and set apart for prophetic ministry through music, including lyres, harps, and cymbals. He was notably chosen second by lot among the singers, indicating a special role in worship within the tribe of Levi. His service was connected to the sacred musical duties assigned to the temple musicians.
namesAndTitles: The name Gedaliah means 'great is YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich proper name. This meaning underscores a recognition of God's greatness, though the name itself was not given directly by God. The biblical reference for this name is found in 1 Chronicles 25:3.
familyAndRelationships: Gedaliah is explicitly identified as the son of Jeduthun, a significant figure connected with temple music. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide additional family details for Gedaliah.
scriptureSignificance: Gedaliah's significance lies in his role within the Levitical musicians, specifically as one chosen by lot to prophesy through musical instruments. This highlights the integration of music and prophecy in worship during the temple period. His selection as second among the singers emphasizes his importance in the liturgical life of Israel as recorded in 1 Chronicles 25.
